featured.title: Three Rulings, Four Days, One Direction: The Supreme Court Just Rewrote Immigration Law
featured.excerpt: Green card holders can be paroled on suspicion. Asylum seekers turned away at the border. TPS terminated without judicial review. A blitz week of 6-3 decisions signals where the court stands — and what Monday's birthright citizenship ruling may bring.
featured.image_caption: The U.S. Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C.
featured.nri_angle: Blanche v. Lau directly weakens the re-entry rights of the 400,000+ Indian-born green card holders who travel to India regularly. The TPS precedent strengthens executive power over discretionary immigration benefits that affect legal immigrants broadly.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Negotiating to Sell Its Fastest Missile to the UAE. The Iran War Made It Possible.
news.excerpt: Talks to export BrahMos and the Akashteer air-defence system mark India's biggest defence pitch to the Gulf — and a direct counter to Pakistan's deepening ties with Saudi Arabia.
news.image_caption: A BrahMos supersonic cruise missile launcher on display during India's Republic Day parade in New Delhi
news.nri_angle: 3.4 million Indians in the UAE stand to benefit from a deeper defence relationship that strengthens bilateral ties and India's strategic standing in the Gulf.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India and the US Say a Trade Deal Is Days Away. Here's What's Actually Holding It Up.
news.excerpt: Greer flew to Delhi, Goyal flew to London, and both sides called it 'very, very close.' But the Supreme Court ruling, Section 301, and a July 24 deadline are making the final stretch harder than the first mile.
news.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who has led trade negotiations with the United States
news.nri_angle: A trade deal would lower tariffs on Indian goods in the U.S. and ease diplomatic tensions affecting visa policy and the business environment for Indian-American entrepreneurs.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: NASA's Chief Just Offered to Help India Build Its Own Space Station. India Hasn't Said Yes.
news.excerpt: Bill Nelson's India visit confirms an ISRO astronaut will fly to the ISS by 2027. The bigger question is whether New Delhi wants American help on the station it plans to build by 2035.
news.image_caption: NASA astronaut Raja Chari with ISRO officials at Johnson Space Center, reflecting deepening US-India space ties
news.nri_angle: Indian-American scientists and engineers at NASA have shaped US space exploration for decades; a deeper ISRO-NASA partnership creates new opportunities for Indian space startups and strengthens the technology bridge between both countries.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Europe's Worst Heatwave on Record Has Killed Over 1,000 in France. Two Million Indians Live in Its Path.
news.excerpt: Scientists say the 40°C-plus temperatures shattering records from Germany to Britain would have been 'virtually impossible' without climate change. The same forces are weakening India's monsoon.
news.image_caption: Satellite thermal image showing hot surface temperatures across Europe during the record-breaking June 2026 heatwave
news.nri_angle: Over two million people of Indian origin live across Europe, concentrated in the UK, Germany, and France — the countries hardest hit by the heatwave. The same climate forces weakening India's monsoon are driving Europe's deadly heat.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Meta Just Paid $900 Million for an Indian Fintech. Its Founder Will Now Run WhatsApp.
news.excerpt: Kunal Shah built CRED from $1 million of his own money into a $4.5 billion company. Now he's taking over the world's biggest messaging platform — and Meta's biggest bet on payments.
news.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED, who will lead WhatsApp globally
news.nri_angle: An Indian founder with no Silicon Valley pedigree now leads one of the world's most important platforms, while the deal reshapes WhatsApp payments for 500 million Indian users.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Biggest Trade Deal Goes Live in 17 Days. It Has Deployed 1,000 People to Make Sure Nobody Misses It.
news.excerpt: The India-UK CETA takes effect on July 15, cutting tariffs on everything from whisky to automobiles. For Indian professionals in Britain, it also means five years of not paying into a pension system they may never use.
news.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who called the UK trade deal India's most comprehensive ever
news.nri_angle: Indian professionals in the UK get a five-year exemption from British social security payments, saving thousands of pounds that can go into tax-free Indian provident funds instead.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Brooklyn Judge Just Told the Trump DOJ It Can't Walk Away From the Adani Case Without Explaining Itself
news.excerpt: Judge Garaufis called the government's motion to dismiss the $250 million bribery indictment 'terse, bland, and conclusory' and ordered prosecutors to justify the decision by July 13
news.image_caption: Gautam Adani, chairman of the Adani Group, faces unresolved criminal charges in a Brooklyn federal court
news.nri_angle: Millions of NRI investors hold Adani Group shares through Indian mutual funds and direct equity; the unresolved US criminal case adds regulatory uncertainty to their portfolios at a time when India-US trade talks are nearing a landmark agreement.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Ireland Beat India for the First Time in Thirty Years of Trying. The World Champions Lost by 34 Runs.
news.excerpt: Belfast's Civil Service Cricket Club hosted one of the biggest upsets in T20I history as Ireland dismantled India's post-World Cup line-up. The second T20I is today.
news.image_caption: India captain Shreyas Iyer, who took over the T20I leadership after Suryakumar Yadav was dropped, faces early scrutiny after the historic defeat in Belfast
news.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian-origin cricket fans in the UK and Ireland follow India's away tours passionately; the historic defeat at a tiny Belfast ground — and the ongoing second T20I today — is a major talking point across diaspora WhatsApp groups and community cricket clubs.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Amazon Just Committed $48 Billion to India. Most of It Will Be Spent Building the AI Infrastructure Indians Haven't Seen Yet.
news.excerpt: CEO Andy Jassy met Modi in New Delhi and announced $13 billion in fresh AI and cloud spending — the largest single technology commitment India has ever received.
news.image_caption: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy, who announced a $48 billion investment commitment to India
news.nri_angle: Indian tech professionals in the US who work at Amazon and AWS now have a concrete reason to consider reverse migration — or at least to watch India's cloud market explode from $48 billion in fresh capital.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Hyderabad Named a Road After Trump. His Own Allies in India Called It Hypocrisy.
news.excerpt: A Congress-ruled state honours the US president with 'Donald Trump Avenue' near the US Consulate — while accusing Modi of being too soft on him.
news.image_caption: US President Donald Trump, who thanked India for naming a Hyderabad road after him
news.nri_angle: For NRIs from Hyderabad — and there are hundreds of thousands of them, particularly in the US tech industry — the irony of their city naming a road after a president who has raised tariffs on Indian goods, whose navy killed Indian sailors, and whose immigration policies threaten H-1B holders is impossible to miss.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Directs ONGC to Build $1.6 Billion Strategic Oil Reserve as Iran War Exposes Eight-Day Vulnerability
news.excerpt: The new underground cavern at Mangaluru would raise India's emergency crude storage by a third, but still leaves the country far short of the IEA's 90-day standard
news.image_caption: An underground strategic petroleum reserve storage facility. India is racing to expand its own crude oil reserves at Mangaluru, Karnataka, after the Iran war exposed its energy vulnerability.
news.image_credit: Wikimedia Commons / US Department of Energy / Public Domain
news.nri_angle: India's energy vulnerability directly affects NRI families through rising fuel and food prices during supply shocks, while the country's $1.6 billion investment signals a strategic shift that could stabilise the economy diaspora investors increasingly count on.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Supreme Court Signs Landmark MOU with Russia on AI in Courts, Drawing Constitutional Scrutiny
news.excerpt: CJI Surya Kant's Moscow agreement promises tech collaboration and judicial exchanges, but legal scholars question whether the court overstepped its constitutional role
news.image_caption: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, who signed the landmark judicial cooperation MOU with Russia's Supreme Court Chairman Igor Krasnov in Moscow on June 24, 2026.
news.nri_angle: The MOU's focus on AI-assisted translation and digital court access could significantly benefit NRIs navigating India's judicial system remotely, while the constitutional debate around the agreement reflects broader questions about institutional boundaries that diaspora legal professionals are closely watching.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Quiet Energy Revolution: Domestic Coal Replaces Imports While Renewables Hit Record 17.9% of Generation
news.excerpt: Power plants designed for imported coal now run on over 50% domestic fuel as solar and wind electricity surges 29% year-on-year, reshaping the country's energy mix
news.image_caption: A thermal power plant in Uttar Pradesh, India. The country is rapidly switching imported coal-based plants to domestic fuel while renewable energy reaches record generation levels.
news.image_credit: Wikimedia Commons / Biswarup Ganguly / CC BY 3.0
news.nri_angle: India's energy transformation has direct implications for NRIs with investments in Indian power companies and the broader economy, as reduced import dependence strengthens the rupee and lowers inflationary pressure on the families they support back home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: He Left Hyderabad With Nothing. Now He's Buying One of India's Biggest Banks for $5 Billion.
news.excerpt: Indian-Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa parked $1 billion in government bonds last week. His Fairfax Financial is closing in on IDBI Bank — the largest foreign investment in an Indian bank ever.
news.image_caption: Prem Watsa, chairman of Fairfax Financial Holdings and an Indian-Canadian billionaire from Hyderabad
news.nri_angle: Prem Watsa, a first-generation Indian-Canadian immigrant from Hyderabad, is making the largest-ever foreign direct investment in an Indian bank — a powerful symbol of diaspora capital flowing home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Is Rationing Cancer Drugs. The FDA Just Called India for Help.
news.excerpt: Hospitals can fill barely a third of their orders for a critical chemotherapy drug. Now the FDA's India office has turned to Cipla, Zydus and at least two other Indian manufacturers to plug the gap.
news.image_caption: Chemotherapy drug infusion components at a hospital — supplies of key cancer drugs like ifosfamide are running critically low across the US
news.nri_angle: Indian pharma companies are being called upon to fill a critical cancer drug shortage in the US — where Indian-origin physicians and pharmacists disproportionately staff the oncology departments now rationing these same drugs.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Housing Market Just Had Its Best Quarter in Years. NRI Buyers Are Leading the Luxury Charge.
news.excerpt: Sales surged 19% across India's top nine cities in Q2 2026, with Bengaluru and Hyderabad leading the boom — and overseas Indians are driving the high-end segment that's propping up the entire market.
news.image_caption: Residential towers rising over Hyderabad, one of India's fastest-growing housing markets in 2026. (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: NRIs are increasingly investing in India's luxury real estate, with favorable exchange rates, post-RERA transparency, and rising prices making Indian property attractive for overseas Indians planning returns, buying for parents, or seeking portfolio diversification.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Iran Just Hit US Bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. Millions of Indians in the Gulf Woke Up to Air-Raid Sirens.
news.excerpt: The ceasefire that was supposed to end the US-Iran war is in freefall. Iran launched missiles and drones at American military sites across the Gulf on Saturday, Trump threatened to erase Iran, and the Strait of Hormuz is being weaponised again.
news.image_caption: An oil tanker loading crude oil at a terminal in the Persian Gulf
news.nri_angle: Over 4.5 million Indians live in Kuwait and Bahrain, the two countries targeted by Iranian strikes. Air-raid sirens and military escalation directly threaten the safety and livelihoods of the Gulf's largest foreign workforce.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Boston Grad, a Dead Cockroach and a 40-Day March. India's Exam Revolt Just Went Mainstream.
news.excerpt: The Cockroach Janta Party started as a meme. Now CNN is at the protest site, Congress is backing a nationwide campaign, and the government is calling students terrorists.
news.image_caption: Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, the historic site where students have been protesting since June 20
news.nri_angle: NRI families watching their children's educational prospects in India dim; the movement's founder is a Boston University graduate who flew back to lead the protests.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Supreme Court Is About to Rule on Whether Babies Born to H-1B Parents Are American Citizens
nri-world.excerpt: A decision expected as early as Monday could strip birthright citizenship from hundreds of thousands of children born each year to parents on temporary visas — including the quarter-million Indians on H-1B status.
nri-world.image_caption: The US Supreme Court building in Washington, where a ruling on birthright citizenship is expected this week
nri-world.nri_angle: This ruling directly affects the quarter-million Indians currently on H-1B visas in America and their families — if upheld, babies born to H-1B holders in the US would not be American citizens, potentially leaving them stateless.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The July 31 Deadline Is Coming. Here's What Every NRI Filing an Indian Tax Return Needs to Know.
nri-world.excerpt: Schedule FA, the DTAA paper trail, the FBAR double bind — a practical guide to the traps that catch diaspora taxpayers every year.
nri-world.image_caption: Tax documents and currency on a desk during filing season
nri-world.nri_angle: Every NRI with Indian income faces the July 31 ITR deadline. The compliance burden is uniquely diaspora-shaped — juggling two tax systems, two sets of forms, and penalties that can reach ₹10 lakh per missed disclosure.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Fifty Years Ago, a Handful of Hare Krishnas Pulled a Chariot Down Fifth Avenue. Now 25,000 Show Up.
nri-world.excerpt: ISKCON's Ratha Yatra in Manhattan just marked its golden anniversary — a milestone in how the Indian diaspora practises faith in public.
nri-world.image_caption: Devotees pull a decorated Ratha Yatra chariot at an ISKCON festival in the United States
nri-world.nri_angle: The Ratha Yatra is the diaspora's most visible public expression of Hindu devotion in the West. For Indian-American families, ISKCON centres have become anchors of cultural continuity — the neighbourhood temple transplanted to Brooklyn and Trafalgar Square.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Modi Wrote in Creole to a Diaspora That Has Been in Seychelles Since Before America Was a Country
nri-world.excerpt: India's prime minister is visiting a 115-island archipelago in the Indian Ocean where Tamil settlers arrived in 1770 — and where Indians now make up nearly a tenth of the population.
nri-world.image_caption: The clock tower in Victoria, Mahé — the capital of Seychelles and the smallest capital city in the world
nri-world.nri_angle: The Indian community in Seychelles is one of the oldest continuous diaspora settlements in the world, yet remains almost invisible to the broader NRI conversation. Modi's visit — and his choice to address them in the local Creole language — underscores how far-flung India's people-to-people ties really are, even in a nation of just 121,000.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Saudi Arabia Just Told 2.4 Million Indians They Can Stop Renting. Few Know What That Actually Means.
nri-world.excerpt: A new digital portal lets foreigners buy property across the Kingdom for the first time — opening the door for millions of Indian workers who have spent decades as tenants in the Gulf's biggest economy.
nri-world.image_caption: The Riyadh skyline — Saudi Arabia's capital and the centre of its expanding real estate market
nri-world.nri_angle: For the 2.4 million Indians living in Saudi Arabia — the largest expatriate group in the Kingdom — the ability to own property transforms the economic equation of Gulf migration from temporary labor to potential long-term investment and stability.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Haldiram's at Leicester Square, Drāvida in the East Village: Indian Restaurants Are Finally Playing Offence Abroad
nri-world.excerpt: An 88-year-old snack empire, a Food Network champion, and two Goa-to-London restaurateurs are betting that the diaspora's food has been undersold for too long.
nri-world.nri_angle: These openings reflect the diaspora's long frustration that the food they actually grew up eating — regional, street-level, migration-shaped — rarely made it onto restaurant menus abroad. The new wave is correcting that.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Son of Indian and Ukrainian Immigrants Is About to Board the ISS. He Brought His Stethoscope.
nri-world.excerpt: NASA astronaut Anil Menon, SpaceX's first flight surgeon and a US Space Force colonel, launches for an eight-month station mission on July 14 — adding a new chapter to the diaspora's quietly growing presence in orbit.
nri-world.image_caption: NASA astronaut Anil Menon in his official flight suit portrait at Johnson Space Center
nri-world.nri_angle: Menon, born to Indian and Ukrainian immigrant parents in Minneapolis, represents the diaspora's expanding footprint beyond corporate boardrooms and into one of the last frontiers. His mission builds on the legacy of Kalpana Chawla, Sunita Williams, and Raja Chari.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Paris Is About to Get Europe's First Traditional Hindu Temple. Thousands of Diaspora Devotees Are Already Packing.
nri-world.excerpt: BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir opens in September with a 13-day Festival of Culture — boat processions on the Seine, Vedic rituals, and a Parisian exhibition that places the temple alongside Notre-Dame.
nri-world.image_caption: Swaminarayan Akshardham in Delhi, built in the same tradition as the upcoming BAPS mandir in Paris
nri-world.nri_angle: The Paris mandir crystallises a pattern the diaspora has been pursuing for two decades: building permanent, architecturally ambitious Hindu sacred spaces abroad — from Robbinsville to Abu Dhabi — that anchor community identity for generations. For NRIs across Europe, it means no longer flying to London or India for a traditional temple experience.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Diaspora Built an American Dream. It Forgot to Plan for Getting Old in It.
nri-world.excerpt: A Queens nonprofit is building robotised food pantries and affordable housing for South Asian seniors. A California volunteer group charges five dollars a class. Across the country, the infrastructure to age with dignity in a foreign land is being improvised from scratch.
nri-world.image_caption: An elderly woman participating in a community yoga session
nri-world.nri_angle: The first large wave of Indian professionals arrived in America after the 1965 Immigration Act. Sixty years later, that cohort is entering its seventies and eighties — in a country whose elder-care infrastructure was not designed for people who speak Gujarati, eat vegetarian, and expect their children to live under the same roof. The story of how the community is scrambling to fill the gap is a defining NRI challenge of this decade.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: America's Oldest Indian Association Just Honoured Seven of Its Own. Four Were Doctors.
nri-world.excerpt: The AIA-NY benefit gala in Flushing celebrated a community's elite — and quietly revealed how narrow the diaspora's definition of success still is, even as a new generation pushes at the edges.
nri-world.image_caption: A Bharatanatyam dancer performs a classical Indian dance on stage, the kind of cultural showcase that anchors diaspora community galas.
nri-world.nri_angle: The honours list of the oldest national Indian-American association is a ritual of self-definition for a community built on professional-visa migration — and a window into whether its founding-era institutions can hold the loyalty of a startup-minded next generation.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Australia Just Honoured Ten Indian-Origin Citizens. None of Them Are Famous.
nri-world.excerpt: The 2026 King's Birthday Honours List reads like a map of how a migrant community embeds itself — through doctors, psychiatrists and the half-century grind of building institutions nobody else would.
nri-world.image_caption: Sydney's skyline, including the Opera House. Indians are now Australia's second-largest migrant community.
nri-world.nri_angle: Honours conferred by the Australian state — not by an Indian-community body — are a signal of belonging, recognising decades of professional and civic service by a migrant population that is now the country's second-largest.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Delhi Spent Years Wanting the Diaspora's Remittances. Now It Wants Its Portfolio.
nri-world.excerpt: A new RBI deposit scheme and the rise of GIFT City are reframing overseas Indians from senders of money home into investors in India — on terms built to compete with Dubai and New York.
nri-world.image_caption: Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City), India's tax-neutral financial hub courting NRI capital
nri-world.nri_angle: Overseas Indians are being courted with hedged, leveraged double-digit returns and tax-efficient GIFT City products that let them treat India as a serious portfolio allocation rather than just a place to send remittances.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is About to Launch the Biggest IPO Wave in Its History — and NRI Investors Are Watching Closely
markets-finance.excerpt: Jio Platforms, the National Stock Exchange, Zepto, and SBI Mutual Fund are among at least ₹90,000 crore worth of public offerings lined up for the second half of 2026, led by what could be India's largest-ever listing
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, the heart of India's capital markets
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors can participate in India's historic IPO wave through NRE/NRO demat accounts; the ₹35,000 crore Jio listing alone could be the largest opportunity in Indian market history.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Tata Motors Is Ramping EV Production by 50% — and Turning to China's Chery to Build Its Premium Electric Future
markets-finance.excerpt: With EV bookings surging 2.5 times on rising fuel costs, Tata is scaling output from 10,000 to 15,000 units a month while licensing Chery's Freelander platform for its delayed Avinya luxury EVs — a strategy that blends domestic manufacturing ambition with quiet Chinese technology dependence.
markets-finance.image_caption: A Tata Nexon EV, the best-selling electric car in India, on display
markets-finance.nri_angle: Tata Motors stock is a bellwether for NRI investors in India's manufacturing story — the EV pivot and Chinese tech dependency create both opportunity and risk for diaspora portfolios.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Doubled Gold Tariffs to Save the Rupee — Now Smugglers Are Filling the Gap
markets-finance.excerpt: A tariff hike from 6% to 15% was meant to staunch an $84 billion gold import bill. Instead, grey-market inflows could hit 100 tons this year, jewellers are pivoting to lighter designs, and NRIs heading home for weddings face painfully higher costs.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold jewellery on display at an Indian jewellery store during the wedding season
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs travelling home for weddings face gold jewellery costs up 10% overnight, and the grey-market discount raises questions about whether to buy at home or abroad — while sovereign gold bonds remain an NRI-friendly alternative.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: South Korea's KOSPI Crashed Twice in a Week — India's Markets Logged a Third Straight Weekly Gain
markets-finance.excerpt: While circuit breakers halted trading in Seoul as Samsung and SK Hynix plummeted over 10 percent in an AI-fuelled rout, India's Nifty and Sensex quietly extended their winning streak, insulated by falling oil prices, RBI measures and a market structure that doesn't bet the house on one sector.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street in Mumbai — home to a market that dodged the global AI selloff this week
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with exposure to both Indian and global markets saw a stark lesson this week: India's diversified index structure and domestic macro tailwinds offered shelter from a tech-driven storm that hammered concentrated bets elsewhere.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Textile Stocks Just Surged — and Brokerages Say the Sector's Best Years Are Ahead
markets-finance.excerpt: Motilal Oswal initiates coverage on eight textile companies with buy ratings and up to 39 percent upside, as cotton duty exemptions, China Plus One sourcing and new free trade deals create a once-in-a-decade opportunity for India's $194 billion textile industry.
markets-finance.image_caption: Workers sorting and folding fabric at a textile factory in India
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors can access India's textile breakout through buy-rated stocks trading at single-digit P/E ratios, with structural growth from China Plus One sourcing and new UK/EU trade deals.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The US Just Asked India to Rescue Its Cancer Patients — and Indian Pharma Stocks Rallied on the News
markets-finance.excerpt: The FDA has reached out to the Indian Drug Manufacturers' Association to find suppliers of ifosfamide, a critical chemotherapy drug in short supply across American hospitals, as India's pharma sector cements its role as the world's backup pharmacy
markets-finance.image_caption: A representative of Cadila Pharmaceuticals, part of the Zydus Group — one of the Indian drugmakers positioned to supply cancer drugs to the US amid a critical shortage
markets-finance.nri_angle: Indian pharma companies like Cipla and Zydus are being directly solicited by the US FDA to supply a life-saving cancer drug, validating the sector's strategic importance and offering NRI investors a structural growth story.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The RBI Just Made Dollar Deposits in India More Rewarding Than They've Been in a Decade — Here's What NRIs Need to Know
markets-finance.excerpt: India's central bank is absorbing all hedging costs on foreign currency deposits, banks are offering 6–7% on the dollar, and leveraged returns could approach 15% — with an estimated $55 billion in inflows by September
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India tower and building complex in Mumbai
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs can earn 6–7% tax-free on dollar deposits in India with zero currency risk under a special RBI window that closes September 30 — leveraged returns could approach 15% for high-net-worth individuals.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Foreign Investors Just Poured a Record $4.2 Billion into Indian Government Bonds — and a Bigger Prize May Be Coming
markets-finance.excerpt: India's bond market is attracting its largest-ever monthly foreign inflow after tax exemptions and expanded access. The real catalyst: potential inclusion in Bloomberg's flagship global bond index, which could unlock $20-30 billion more.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Kolkata, reflecting in the waters of Lal Dighi
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRI investors, the bond market reforms — combined with tax exemptions and the ongoing FCNR-B deposit push — create a rare window to earn attractive returns on Indian sovereign debt with reduced currency and tax risk.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Pharma Industry Is Betting Its Future on Biosimilars — and the Numbers Suggest the Gamble May Pay Off
markets-finance.excerpt: With $30 billion in annual exports, the most USFDA-approved plants outside America, and a biosimilars market projected to quadruple by 2033, India's 'Pharmacy of the World' is rewriting its playbook — from cheap generics to high-value biologics.
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors and Indian-origin pharma professionals in the US and UK are watching India's shift from generics to biosimilars closely — it creates both portfolio opportunities in listed Indian pharma stocks and career pathways for reverse-brain-drain talent.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: A Hyderabad-Born Billionaire Bets $1 Billion on India — and May Finally Buy IDBI Bank
markets-finance.excerpt: Prem Watsa's Fairfax Financial parked nearly $1 billion in Indian bonds in a single week, signaling the four-year IDBI privatisation saga is nearing a close
markets-finance.image_caption: Prem Watsa, founder of Fairfax Financial Holdings and the Indian-Canadian billionaire bidding for IDBI Bank
markets-finance.nri_angle: A Hyderabad-born billionaire could complete India's largest-ever foreign bank acquisition — testing whether India can actually privatise a public-sector bank, and showcasing the bond-market tax breaks designed to attract NRI capital.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Oil Crashes to Pre-War Levels as Saudi Exports Resume — and India Gets a $40-a-Barrel Windfall
markets-finance.excerpt: Brent crude plunged 11% in a week to $72 as tankers flooded through the Strait of Hormuz, handing India's economy its best macro news in four months.
markets-finance.image_caption: An oil tanker off the coast near the Gulf shipping lanes that were disrupted during the Iran war
markets-finance.nri_angle: Lower oil strengthens the rupee and India equities, improves corporate margins, and gives RBI room to keep rates accommodative — directly benefiting NRI portfolios.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Amazon Pledges Another $13 Billion to India, Betting the Country Becomes a Global AI Hub
markets-finance.excerpt: Andy Jassy’s meeting with Narendra Modi capped a fresh commitment that lifts Amazon’s planned 2026–30 India spend to $48 billion — the latest and largest move in a hyperscaler land grab that is quietly turning India into critical infrastructure for the AI age.
markets-finance.image_caption: Amazon's fresh $13 billion pledge will expand AWS data-centre capacity in Mumbai and Hyderabad, part of a hyperscaler push into India's AI economy
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs — many of them the engineers, founders and investors of the global tech economy — a wave of hyperscaler capital landing in Mumbai and Hyderabad reshapes the calculus of where careers, startups and portfolios should be anchored: the AI infrastructure they have helped build in Seattle and the Bay Area is now being poured into the country many of them came from, narrowing the distance between the diaspora’s two homes.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Ben Stokes Retires. The Man Who Defined a Generation of England Cricket — and Haunted India Along the Way.
sports.excerpt: The 35-year-old all-rounder announced his retirement mid-match at Trent Bridge, then took a wicket with his first ball and opened the batting with two sixes. For Indian cricket fans, he was the rival you couldn't look away from.
sports.image_caption: Ben Stokes in England Test whites during his time as captain
sports.nri_angle: Stokes defined England-India cricket rivalry for a decade — from World Cup heroics to Bazball Test battles, NRIs in England and Indian fans worldwide watched him as the rival they couldn't look away from.

sports.title: 356 and Counting. Deepti Sharma Is Now the Greatest Wicket-Taker in Women's International Cricket History.

sports.image_caption: Deepti Sharma during an international match in 2025
sports.nri_angle: Deepti Sharma is now the most prolific wicket-taker in women's international cricket history — a milestone witnessed by NRIs at Lord's, with Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma in the stands, marking how far Indian women's cricket has come.

sports.title: Two Runs Short at Lord's. Harmanpreet's Heroics Weren't Enough to Save India's World Cup.

sports.title: Lindblad Finishes P10 in Austria. India's Closest Thing to an F1 Driver Just Keeps Collecting Points.

sports.title: Swept in Belfast. Ireland Inflict India's First Bilateral T20I Series Loss in Over Two Years.

sports.image_caption: Kidambi Srikanth in action during a BWF World Tour event

The debate over his future touches on the deep emotional bond between the diaspora and Indian cricket's biggest names, and raises questions about whether the next generation can carry the same weight for fans watching from abroad.

technology.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai's Google now controls AI infrastructure so essential that even Meta must queue for access — a power shift felt daily by tens of thousands of Indian engineers at both companies, and one driving the hyperscaler data centre race in India.

technology.nri_angle: NRIs dealing with India's notoriously slow legal system — property disputes, inheritance claims, business litigation — stand to benefit as legal AI compresses the hours (and bills) lawyers spend on document review and case research.

technology.title: India's Government Built Its Own GPT. It Speaks 22 Languages. The Talent to Scale It Lives Abroad.

technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI researchers dominate Silicon Valley labs but India's own sovereign AI push faces a severe talent deficit — BharatGen's success may depend on whether NRI talent can be channelled back through sabbaticals, advisory roles or returns.

technology.nri_angle: NRI semiconductor professionals considering a return to India's chip industry face new timeline uncertainty. Diaspora investors bullish on Tata Group's fab ambitions should factor in geopolitical supply risks.

lifestyle-health.title: The HPV Vaccine Has Reduced Cervical Cancer Deaths to Zero in Young Women — and India Is Finally Racing to Catch Up
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark Lancet study finds 100% reduction in cervical cancer deaths among vaccinated women in England, while India — home to a quarter of the world's cervical cancer fatalities — launches its largest-ever immunisation drive
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Gardasil HPV vaccine syringe — the vaccine has been shown to eliminate cervical cancer deaths among young women in a landmark Lancet study (Whispyhistory / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: India accounts for 25% of global cervical cancer deaths; NRI families should ensure children receive the HPV vaccine, which the new Lancet study shows reduces cervical cancer mortality to zero when given before age 14.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Any Amount of Alcohol Raises Dementia Risk, a Massive New Study Confirms — and the "One Drink Is Fine" Belief Was an Illusion
lifestyle-health.excerpt: An Oxford-Yale-Cambridge-Harvard analysis of 560,000 adults and genetic data from 2.4 million people finds no safe level of drinking for brain health, while a separate Nature Health study links alcohol to 20 chronic conditions including multiple cancers
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Research now shows any level of alcohol consumption poses risks to brain health
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian drinking culture is normalising in the diaspora, but the new Oxford-Harvard genetic study shows no safe level of alcohol for brain health — particularly concerning given South Asians' elevated baseline risk for metabolic disease and dementia.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Women Who Took the Pill in Their Twenties Had Larger, Healthier Brains Decades Later
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new MRI study of 459 women aged 65 to 80 found that a history of hormonal birth control was linked to greater gray matter volume in brain regions tied to memory and cognition — adding to evidence that lifetime estrogen exposure may shape how the brain ages.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An MRI scan of the human brain, the imaging technique used in the study linking oral contraceptive use to increased gray matter volume (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian women face a higher baseline risk for dementia and often navigate cultural taboos around contraception — this study reframes a common reproductive decision as a potential long-term brain-health advantage.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Eating Only Between 8 AM and 2 PM for Two Weeks Reduced Heart Inflammation in Heart Attack Survivors
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A randomised crossover trial published in the Journal of the American Heart Association found that a strict six-hour eating window lowered neutrophil counts, shifted monocyte gene expression toward anti-inflammatory patterns, and cut low-grade systemic inflammation in patients with established coronary artery disease.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A CT coronary artery scan of the type used to image cardiovascular disease in clinical settings
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians have among the highest rates of premature heart disease worldwide — this study suggests a no-cost, no-drug dietary timing strategy that could complement standard cardiac rehab.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: An Anti-Inflammatory Diet Cut Dementia Risk by Up to 29% — Even in People Already Showing Alzheimer's Signs
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A 15-year study of nearly 2,000 older adults found that eating to cool inflammation helped the most in those whose blood already carried Alzheimer's biomarkers — and the foods that worked are staples of the Indian kitchen.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fresh vegetables, fruits, nuts, and whole grains — the building blocks of an anti-inflammatory diet linked to lower dementia risk
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry 2–4× higher rates of Type 2 diabetes and chronic inflammation, making anti-inflammatory eating especially relevant — and many staples of the Indian kitchen already fit this pattern.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Walking Speed May Predict How Long You Live — and a Few Simple Changes Can Help
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Large-scale studies link brisk walking to up to 43 percent lower mortality risk, while slower stepping speed signals hidden health declines that diaspora families should watch for in ageing parents.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A person walking along a tree-lined autumn pathway — walking speed is increasingly recognised as a powerful predictor of longevity. Photo: Masood Aslami / Pexels
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For NRIs with ageing parents in India, a simple walking-speed check during video calls or visits can flag health risks long before a diagnosis — and brisk walking is free preventive medicine anywhere in the world.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Exercise Alone Can Tackle Six of the 14 Known Dementia Risk Factors — and South Asians Stand to Gain the Most
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A University of Minnesota review finds that consistent physical activity can prevent or delay up to half of all dementia cases by managing obesity, hypertension, diabetes, depression, cholesterol and inactivity — the very conditions that disproportionately affect the Indian diaspora.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An older adult running on a stadium track — the kind of regular physical activity that new research links to dramatically lower dementia risk
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry elevated rates of diabetes, hypertension and metabolic syndrome — the exact modifiable risk factors that exercise directly addresses — making this research especially relevant for NRI families watching parents and grandparents age.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Desk Job May Need 13,000 Steps to Undo — but Even 1,700 Can Start to Fight Back
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark NIH-funded study using Fitbit data from 6,000 adults maps exactly how many daily steps it takes to offset the metabolic damage of sitting 8 to 14 hours a day — findings that hit especially close to home for diaspora tech workers.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Walking even a modest number of extra steps each day can offset the health risks of prolonged sitting
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian tech workers in the US sit 10-12 hours daily and carry higher genetic risk for diabetes and heart disease — this study maps the exact step counts needed to fight back.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Vaping While You Smoke May Nearly Triple Your Risk of Early-Onset Lung Cancer, Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: An Ohio State study of more than 3,000 young adults found that those who both vaped and smoked had 2.8 times the lung cancer risk of smokers who never vaped — a finding with sharp relevance for diaspora youth abroad
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An e-cigarette device — the study found dual vaping and smoking dramatically raises lung cancer risk in under-50 adults
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: India banned e-cigarettes in 2019, but millions of young NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada vape freely — and this study shows that if they also smoke, their lung cancer risk nearly triples.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Snacks Your Children Eat May Be Feeding Their Anxiety — and Multiple Studies Now Show a Dose-Dependent Link
lifestyle-health.excerpt: New research finds adolescents who consume the most ultra-processed food have nearly four times the odds of depression and nearly double the odds of anxiety — a pattern with pointed implications for diaspora families raising children on Western diets
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Ultra-processed packaged foods — multiple studies now link heavy consumption to depression, anxiety, and stress in young people
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian children raised in the US, UK, and Canada eat far more ultra-processed food than their parents did in India — and new research draws a direct, dose-dependent line between UPF intake and depression, anxiety, and stress in youth.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Nearly Half of Adults Over 65 Actually Got Sharper or Stronger — and Their Mindset Made the Difference
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Yale study tracking 11,000 older Americans for 12 years found that positive beliefs about aging were strongly linked to measurable improvements in cognition and walking speed
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An older couple walking together outdoors — walking speed is considered a vital sign by geriatricians
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian culture's reverence for elders may have biological backing — positive aging attitudes predict measurable cognitive and physical gains, a counterweight for NRI families navigating Western decline-focused medical frameworks.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Grandmother's Haldi Was Ahead of the Science — Curcumin Now Shows It Can Ease Gut Trouble and Trim the Waistline
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new clinical trial finds that 1,500 mg of curcumin daily reduced bloating, constipation, and BMI in women with severe obesity — adding to a growing body of evidence that the golden spice does more than season a curry.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fresh turmeric root and ground turmeric powder, the source of the bioactive compound curcumin
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Turmeric has been central to South Asian kitchens and home remedies for generations — this research validates what Indian grandmothers have long believed, and offers NRIs a familiar, accessible strategy for digestive health.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From Udupi to the Pacific Northwest: Hari Nayak Plots Indian Cuisine's Next Frontier
food.excerpt: The Michelin-recognised chef is opening a new restaurant at Woodinville's Harvest Yard that filters India's culinary traditions through the bounty of the Pacific Northwest.
food.image_caption: A masala dosa, the classic South Indian dish from the Udupi tradition that shaped chef Hari Nayak's culinary philosophy (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: A Michelin-star Indian chef opening in the Pacific Northwest gives the large Seattle-area Indian American community a fine-dining destination that redefines Indian cuisine beyond neighbourhood curry houses.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Butter Chicken at Costco: How Indian Food Brands Are Storming America's Grocery Aisles
food.excerpt: From Quicklly's launch at 2,500 ALDI stores to Truly Indian's NEXTY Award nods, packaged Indian cuisine is muscling into mainstream American retail at an unprecedented pace.
food.image_caption: Butter chicken served with butter naan, the iconic dish now available across American grocery chains from Costco to Trader Joe's (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: Butter chicken and tikka masala naan at Costco and ALDI represent a cultural milestone for Indian Americans who have long wished for their staple foods in mainstream American grocery stores.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Copper and Courage: How a Punjabi Family Rebuilt Their Las Vegas Restaurant and Earned a James Beard Nod
food.excerpt: When the Dhillon family's beloved Indian restaurant was demolished with the Hawaiian Marketplace, their son brought it back — and in its first year, Tamba became a James Beard Best New Restaurant finalist.
food.image_caption: An Indian dinner spread at a restaurant, featuring curry, rice, and traditional accompaniments
food.nri_angle: The Dhillon family's journey from Punjabi immigrants running a small Monterey restaurant in 1989 to James Beard Best New Restaurant finalists in Las Vegas mirrors the broader Indian American story of ambition and cultural pride.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From Chicago's Michelin Star to Phoenix and Hudson Yards: The Sujan Sarkar Playbook
food.excerpt: The Kolkata-born chef behind Indienne is building a multi-city, multi-concept Indian restaurant empire — and mentoring the next generation of desi chefs along the way.
food.image_caption: The Michelin Guide — Chef Sujan Sarkar's Indienne in Chicago holds a coveted Michelin star (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: Indian American chef Sujan Sarkar is building what may become the first Michelin-scale Indian restaurant empire in the US, proving that desi cuisine belongs at every level of American dining.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Your Chai Just Got Cheaper: India Wins Zero-Duty Tea Access to America
food.excerpt: A tariff breakthrough gives Indian tea exporters an edge over China just as a wave of Asian tea brands floods the US market.
food.image_caption: A glass of freshly brewed masala chai served in a traditional Indian style
food.nri_angle: Zero-duty tariffs on Indian tea could make authentic chai more accessible and affordable for NRIs while helping Indian brands compete against Chinese tea chains flooding the US market.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Mango Diplomacy: How India's Embassies Are Making America Fall for the King of Fruits
food.excerpt: From Costco aisles to Dupont Circle tents, Indian mangoes are selling out faster than they arrive — powered by NRI nostalgia and a quiet diplomatic push.
food.image_caption: Ripe mangoes, whole and halved, showing golden flesh
food.nri_angle: For 4.8 million Indian Americans, Indian mangoes are an annual emotional lifeline to home — and now embassies and Costco are making them accessible.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: The Quiet Rise of the Biryani Belt: How One Franchise Built 50 Outposts Across America
food.excerpt: Bawarchi Biryanis, run almost entirely by Telugu-American families, has become the largest Indian restaurant franchise in the US — and just opened inside a Colorado hotel.
food.image_caption: A plate of mutton biryani served with accompaniments
food.nri_angle: The Bawarchi franchise story is the Telugu-American diaspora story — families bringing Hyderabadi biryani to every American metro where their community has settled.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From Michelin Stars to Street Rolls: Indian Restaurants Claim New American Ground
food.excerpt: A wave of openings — from a James Beard semifinalist in Phoenix to Kolkata street food in Jersey City — signals that Indian cuisine's US expansion is accelerating faster than ever.
food.image_caption: An elaborate spread of regional Indian dishes — from Michelin-starred restaurants to street-food icons, Indian cuisine is claiming new ground across America (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: Indian restaurants are no longer clustering in coastal enclaves — they're planting flags in Phoenix, Fort Collins, and the Hudson Valley, following the diaspora into America's interior.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Grandma's Haldi, America's 'Herb of the Year': Turmeric's Golden Coronation
food.excerpt: The International Herb Association has named turmeric its 2026 Herb of the Year, a recognition that would surprise exactly zero Indian grandmothers.
food.image_caption: Vibrant turmeric powder spelled out in golden yellow on a dark surface
food.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up with haldi doodh as the cure for everything, watching turmeric become a $1 billion wellness ingredient in the West is both validating and a little surreal.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Doubles, Bunny Chow, and Idli Shrimp: Drāvida Maps the Diaspora's Forgotten Food Routes
food.excerpt: Chef Aarthi Sampath's new East Village restaurant doesn't just serve Indian food — it traces how Indian flavours migrated across the Caribbean, Africa, and Southeast Asia.
food.image_caption: A golden crispy masala dosa served with coconut chutney and sambar
food.nri_angle: Drāvida's menu is a mirror for NRIs: it asks what happens to food when people migrate, and whether the dishes that evolved in Trinidad, South Africa, and Malaysia are as 'Indian' as the originals.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Beyond Tikka Masala: Kerala's Coconut-and-Curry-Leaf Cuisine Stakes Its Claim in America
food.excerpt: Datassential named Keralan food a 'Cuisine to Know for 2026' as coconut-forward South Indian restaurants multiply across major U.S. metros.
food.image_caption: Appam, a soft fermented rice pancake, served with a coconut-milk vegetable stew, a classic Kerala breakfast.
food.nri_angle: For Malayali and South Indian families abroad, seeing home-state dishes like appam, stew and the banana-leaf sadya celebrated at buzzed-about U.S. restaurants is a long-awaited vindication.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: The Patel Brothers Effect: America's Largest Indian Grocer Bets on the Suburbs
food.excerpt: As the chain breaks ground on new suburban megastores, NRI grocery demand is shifting from basic staples to region-specific snacks, festival sweets and Ayurvedic goods.
food.image_caption: A Patel Brothers store in Hicksville, New York; the chain is America's largest Indian grocer (Wikimedia Commons).
food.nri_angle: A new Patel Brothers within driving distance spares NRI families long pilgrimages to big-city Indian quarters and signals their suburb has hit a demographic tipping point.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: India Is Negotiating to Sell Its Fastest Missile to the UAE. The Iran War Made It Possible.
carousel.excerpt: Talks to export BrahMos and the Akashteer air-defence system mark India's biggest defence pitch to the Gulf — and a direct counter to Pakistan's deepening ties with Saudi Arabia.
carousel.image_caption: A BrahMos supersonic cruise missile launcher on display during India's Republic Day parade in New Delhi
carousel.nri_angle: 3.4 million Indians in the UAE stand to benefit from a deeper defence relationship that strengthens bilateral ties and India's strategic standing in the Gulf.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: He Was the Hero for 30 Years — Now Akshay Kumar Plays the Monster in Priyadarshan's 'Haiwaan'
carousel.excerpt: Saif Ali Khan as a blind man hunted by a psychopath, Kajol, Bobby Deol, Mohanlal's surprise cameo, and the filmmaker who just made ₹293 crore with 'Bhooth Bangla' — all arriving September 11
carousel.image_caption: Akshay Kumar, who plays a villain for the first time in Priyadarshan's Haiwaan (Wikimedia Commons)
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Ben Stokes Retires. The Man Who Defined a Generation of England Cricket — and Haunted India Along the Way.
carousel.excerpt: The 35-year-old all-rounder announced his retirement mid-match at Trent Bridge, then took a wicket with his first ball and opened the batting with two sixes. For Indian cricket fans, he was the rival you couldn't look away from.
carousel.image_caption: Ben Stokes in England Test whites during his time as captain
carousel.nri_angle: Stokes defined England-India cricket rivalry for a decade — from World Cup heroics to Bazball Test battles, NRIs in England and Indian fans worldwide watched him as the rival they couldn't look away from.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Pichai's Google Just Told Meta to Get in Line. The AI Compute War Has a Waitlist.
carousel.excerpt: Google has restricted Meta's access to Gemini AI models after Zuckerberg's team demanded more computing capacity than Alphabet could deliver. For Indian engineers at both companies, the rationing is reshaping daily work.
carousel.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet and Google, in 2023
carousel.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai's Google now controls AI infrastructure so essential that even Meta must queue for access — a power shift felt daily by tens of thousands of Indian engineers at both companies, and one driving the hyperscaler data centre race in India.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: India Is About to Launch the Biggest IPO Wave in Its History — and NRI Investors Are Watching Closely
carousel.excerpt: Jio Platforms, the National Stock Exchange, Zepto, and SBI Mutual Fund are among at least ₹90,000 crore worth of public offerings lined up for the second half of 2026, led by what could be India's largest-ever listing
carousel.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, the heart of India's capital markets
carousel.nri_angle: NRI investors can participate in India's historic IPO wave through NRE/NRO demat accounts; the ₹35,000 crore Jio listing alone could be the largest opportunity in Indian market history.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk
